name: NA64

facility_roles.quote: electron beam of 100-150 GeV energy from the Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS)
facility_roles.note: Beam delivered via the H4 beamline, which CERN's own Experimental Areas page confirms is located inside EHN1 in the North Area.

intervals.label: approved (CERN Research Board)
intervals.locator: na64.web.cern.ch: 'Approved for A' invisible decay searches January 2016' / 'Official CERN Research Board approval: March 9, 2016'

intervals.label: operating
intervals.quote: started operations at CERN's North Area in 2016

physics_goals.value: Search for dark photons, light dark bosons (Z') and other dark-sector particles, and for invisible decays of neutral mesons, using the active beam-dump / missing-energy technique

unique_capabilities.value: Active beam-dump and missing-energy technique whose sensitivity to a hidden Z' coupling scales as epsilon^2 rather than epsilon^4 as in classical beam-dump searches

summary.plain: NA64 is a CERN experiment that fires an electron beam into a block of material and watches for missing energy -- a sign that an invisible, unknown particle escaped. It searches for dark photons and other hidden particles.
summary.technical: Fixed-target active beam-dump experiment on the H4 beamline in EHN1 (CERN North Area SPS beam), using 100-150 GeV electrons (with planned muon/hadron beam extensions) and the missing-energy technique to search for dark photons, dark leptonic gauge bosons and invisible meson decays. Proposed January 2014, approved by the CERN Research Board 9 March 2016, operating since 2016.

notes: Derived fields (detector_ids, site_ids, result_ids, document_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).
